name: Sage 200
description: Read Sage 200 Standard and Professional through the Sage 200 API: customers, suppliers, sales and purchase orders, posted invoices, credit notes and payments, stock items and stock levels, nominal codes. Sage ID OAuth 2.0, read-only.
prerequisites: Sage issues the OAuth client ID and secret on request: write to Sage Developer Services (developers.programme@sage.com) and complete their form; it takes a few days and cannot be done inside Sage 200. You also need a developer subscription key from the Sage Developer Portal and a Sage ID that is an API user of your companies.
instructions:
**What this connects to**: the Sage 200 API (Sage 200 Standard, and Sage 200 Professional connected to the API), `https://api.columbus.sage.com/uk/<product>/accounts/v1`. It reads customers, suppliers, sales and purchase orders, posted sales and purchase transactions (invoices, credit notes, receipts, payments), stock items and stock levels, and nominal codes. This first version only reads.

**Start with `sage_200_list_sites`**: it lists the sites and companies the signed-in user can reach. Every other tool takes `site_id` and `company_id` from it; they are sent as the `X-Site` and `X-Company` headers Sage 200 requires.

**Setup**
1. Client credentials are issued by Sage, not created in Sage 200: request them from Sage Developer Services (developers.programme@sage.com, then Sage's application form). Choose a confidential (web server) client with the redirect URI `<your AnythingMCP URL>/api/mcp-oauth/callback` (on AnythingMCP Cloud: `https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/api/mcp-oauth/callback`). Sage takes a few days.
2. In the Sage Developer Portal, get a developer subscription key (primary key) for the Sage 200 API.
3. Set `SAGE200_PRODUCT` to `sage200` for Sage 200 Standard or `sage200extra` for Sage 200 Professional, and fill in client ID, client secret and subscription key.
4. On the connector page, click **Authorize with Provider** and sign in with the Sage ID that is an API user of your Sage 200 companies (for Sage 200 Professional, the company must be connected to the API in System Administration).

**Querying**: lists take OData options: `filter` (e.g. `reference eq 'ABC001'`), `select`, `orderby`, `top`, `skip`. Field names are snake_case, as in the answers. Ids are numbers and differ from references and codes.

**Invoices**: posted invoices and credit notes are ledger transactions; read them with `sage_200_list_sales_transactions` / `sage_200_list_purchase_transactions` and filter on the transaction type and outstanding value.

**Pitfalls**: 401 means the Sage ID token is not valid (authorize again) or the subscription key is wrong; 403 means the Sage ID is not an API user of that company. Amounts are in the account's currency; check `currency_id`.

SAGE200_PRODUCT.label: Sage 200 edition
SAGE200_PRODUCT.help: sage200 for Sage 200 Standard, sage200extra for Sage 200 Professional.

SAGE200_CLIENT_ID.label: OAuth client ID
SAGE200_CLIENT_ID.help: The client ID Sage Developer Services issued for your application.

SAGE200_CLIENT_SECRET.label: OAuth client secret
SAGE200_CLIENT_SECRET.help: The client secret issued with it (confidential web server client).

SAGE200_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY.label: API subscription key
SAGE200_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY.help: Sage Developer Portal > your profile > subscriptions: the primary key of your Sage 200 API subscription. Sent as Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key.

verifyHints.401: Sage 200 refused the call. Authorize the connector again with a Sage ID that is an API user, and check the subscription key and the edition (sage200 or sage200extra).
verifyHints.403: The Sage ID is not an API user of this site or company. Add it in Sage 200 (System Administration or the Sage 200 Standard settings).
verifyHints.404: Not found on the Sage 200 API. Check the edition: sage200 for Standard, sage200extra for Professional.

tools.name: sage_200_list_sites
tools.description: The Sage 200 sites and companies the signed-in Sage ID user can reach through the API, with site_id, site name, company_id and company name. Start here: every other tool needs a site id and a company id.

tools.name: sage_200_list_customers
tools.description: Customer accounts with id, reference, name, balance, credit limit, on-hold flag, account status, currency and contact details. Filter by reference or name; use the id for get_customer or to filter orders and transactions.

site_id.description: Site id from sage_200_list_sites (site_id). Sent as the X-Site header.

company_id.description: Company id from sage_200_list_sites (company_id within the site). Sent as the X-Company header.

filter.description: OData $filter on the resource's fields, e.g. reference eq 'ABC001' or date ge 2026-01-01. Strings in single quotes.

orderby.description: OData $orderby, e.g. reference asc or date desc.
